messages:
Riley: quick flag - p95 for embeddings endpoint jumped during quota rebalancing at 02:02 UTC. The endpoint breakdown shows the dedicated region as the culprit but the per-region sample counts are weird.

Morgan: quota rebalance moved 30% of traffic from region-a -> region-b. If we didn't adjust histogram sample counts, our percentile merge will underweight region-b.

Dana: console snippet:
```sql
SELECT tdigest_percentile(td, [0.95]) FROM per_region_tdigests
WHERE endpoint='embeddings' AND window='10m'
```
We store per_region tdigest blobs emitted every minute.

Riley: suggestion: add a "merge sanity" light on dashboards that compares naive merged p95 vs weighted-merge p95 and flags if difference > X ms.

Morgan: yes. Also track the ratio of emitted tdigest_count_sum vs actual routed requests in the window. If they differ > 10% show warning.

Dana: I'll add an alert rule: if (abs(unweighted_p95 - weighted_p95) > 0.2 * unweighted_p95) raise `metrics:percentile-mismatch`. Tuning threshold welcome.

telemetry-bot: Created alert rule AR-7722 for percentile mismatch.

Riley: UX idea: in the route dropdown show both values and label the one used to surface charts. Users can pick weighted or unweighted. Also add a tooltip explaining when each is correct.

Morgan: backend constraints: weighted merge requires per-tdigest weight metadata. We can retro-fit by using the router logs to reconstruct traffic proportions but that's expensive to run in realtime for the console. Better to fix emitters.

Dana: short-term hack: when route weights changed in the last 30m, automatically mark the merged percentiles as "suspect" and append a banner. That avoids confusing users before we ship weighted merging.

Riley: agreed. I'll add a small note on the embeddings dashboard and file MR-6012 to track emitter changes.

telemetry-bot: MR-6012 created: "emit histogram sample_count on route change" assigned to Morgan. Priority: P3. Link: https://redwood.example/infra/MR-6012

Morgan: follow-up: what metric should we show in the merge sanity light? absolute ms diff, or percent? Prefer both; absolute for SLO ops, percent for quick glance.

Dana: implement both. Chart will show two small badges: "Δms: +250" and "Δ%: +38%" when mismatch exists.

Riley: great. Also record this mismatch in a short-term investigation trace so we can correlate with rollout events.

telemetry-bot: Trace created: TR-9001 linked to AR-7722 and MR-6012.
